studies.name: Sybil scaling
studies.result: With strong checks at 972 identities, Sonnet specialist accuracy rose from 47.2% with 4 checks to 100% with 108 checks: +52.8 percentage points (descriptive 95% interval +38.9 to +66.7). Haiku showed +51.4 points on identical packets.
studies.sample: 24 paired world roots; 2,400 valid Sonnet outputs. Identities and outputs are not independent worlds.
studies.reading: A replicated checking/admission effect. These are scripted identities feeding one model synthesizer, not 972 autonomous agents.
studies.limit: One graph family, repeated easy facts, two related model families/configurations. A ceiling bootstrap interval is not a reliability guarantee.
studies.next: Change the scarcity and independence of evidence, and compare admission policies at equal cost.

studies.name: Sybil verification budget
studies.result: Only 7 of 120 cells met both ≥90% specialist accuracy and ≤5% attacker seats; all used 10% attacker check-pass probability. At N=324, coverage with 32→108 checks raised accuracy 97.2→100%, but attacker seats also rose 1.98→10.70%.
studies.sample: 24 fresh paired roots ×120 cells = 2,880/2,880 valid outputs.
studies.reading: More checks are not monotonically safer. Accuracy can conceal malicious admission and exclusion of honest specialists. Random checking can outperform coverage at a matched budget.
studies.limit: Exploratory point-mean targets, unadjusted grid search, repeated facts and synthetic independent checks. Historical immutable preregistration receipt is missing.
studies.next: Report accuracy, attacker share and honest retention together; test nonredundant specialist facts.

studies.name: Sybil newcomers
studies.result: Under the round-eight sleeper attack, Sonnet accuracy was 25.0% for random checking, 19.4% for renewal and 8.3% for reputation. Renewal minus reputation: +11.1 points, interval touching zero. Policy ranking barely changed from Haiku.
studies.reading: When truthful evidence is scarce, the optimistic recovery story weakens. The admission-bottleneck explanation is plausible, rather than separately established by manipulation.
studies.limit: The identity-splitting contrast itself remains inconclusive; do not confuse an attack effect with a demonstrated amplification from additional identities.
studies.next: Hold attacker resources fixed while varying identities and evidence admission.

studies.name: Market splitting · Sonnet
studies.result: The flexible owner split into another firm and sustained evasion in 6/6 firm-regulated markets, versus 0/6 owner-regulated and 0/6 unregulated markets. Mean profit improvement against the locked-firm control was 15.89%.
studies.sample: Six related task clusters; 36/36 valid episodes; one sampled trajectory per condition.
studies.reading: In this simulator, attaching the rule to firm identity gives the agent an incentive to split; attaching it to the common owner removes that observed behavior.
studies.limit: One model-controlled owner, scripted rivals, selected model/interface after earlier failures. Six successes do not establish a universal evasion rate.
studies.next: Finish the fresh-market Opus replication, then test independent market structures.

studies.name: Phantom Coast PC2
studies.result: With misleading reports and no audit, teams covered 2.50 distinct cells in 12 sensing slots; single agents 3.25; uniform sampling 12. All directly inspected cells were classified correctly. The audit's team upper-error improvement was 3.13 points, below the 5.56-point practical threshold.
studies.sample: Eight roots, 96 complete episodes, 1,792 requests: 1,791 valid and one invalid.
studies.reading: Repetitive acquisition is the clearest observed failure. Three proposals did not make the group explore effectively.
studies.limit: Unknown cells dominate the error bounds. Upper error is not observed misclassification. The proposed avoidance interaction has opposing family signs; compute differs across policies.
studies.next: The separately designed coverage-guard PC3 is running; wait for its full result.

studies.name: Capture and memory mix · Qwen MP3
studies.result: After purge, original-convention share was 37.5% with pure short memory, 1.0% with pure full memory, and 9.4%, 15.6%, 22.9% in the three mixtures. Pure short fully recovered 2/12; each mixture 0/12.
studies.sample: 12 tasks per memory condition; paired arms. Checked A1 endpoints from saved records.
studies.reading: The Qwen result favors pure short memory. The earlier mixture benefit is model-dependent; the proposed moderator is a post-hoc lead.
studies.limit: Reporting needs correction: 327 raw records with 127 invalid become 180 selected records (178 valid) through last-valid selection. README discloses redos, table footer says no retries; table says round 50 while configuration says 30. One hub capture fraction exceeds 1.
studies.next: Reconcile attempt lineage, retry accounting and captions before presenting combined cross-model claims.

studies.name: Right Dissenter RD4
studies.verdict: Narrow memory benefit; no gate gain
studies.result: Original and symmetric learned gates each achieved 87/96 acceptable decisions; always-check 88/96. All 59 retained native closures preserved the correct action without new calls or checks.
studies.sample: 24 roots, 576 assigned decisions; transport sensitivity overlaps.
studies.reading: Decision memory can preserve tested correct closures. Recovery wording did not improve overall outcomes.
studies.limit: One-point outcome differences do not rank the methods reliably. The learned gate saved three checks but added 37–38 logical calls.
studies.next: Fix repeated deferral consuming the later recovery budget; assess total cost rather than check count alone.

studies.name: Discussion D1 · Opus configuration
studies.result: All 72 calls valid. Fresh clean full-evidence decisions: 12/12 justified. Reused clean tasks: 6/6 correct, against Haiku 2/6 and Sonnet 3/6. Report-only quorums still 4/6; unnecessary abstentions 8/18; all six supported false memories were inherited.
studies.sample: 12 fresh clean cases plus reused development conditions; 72 calls are not 72 independent tasks.
studies.reading: This configuration can solve the clean task. It still cannot recover absent truth from a restricted, misleading evidence set.
studies.limit: Model, thinking allowance, output cap and sampling changed together. Fresh clean qualification is not fresh full-swarm qualification or a discussion-dose effect.
studies.next: Qualify the full report/swarm pathway on fresh worlds before the main comparison.

studies.name: Compositional safety Q0-007
studies.result: 24/24 valid safe completions, zero violations; both centralized and four-role configurations passed.
studies.sample: Six new structural templates; 24 qualification episodes; 178 model calls.
studies.reading: A meaningful recovery from earlier baseline failures. The current configuration is capable of the qualification tasks.
studies.limit: Roots and settings differ from historical models. This is not a model-only safety comparison and does not show that receipts improve safety.
studies.next: Q0-008 is running after budget-binding changes; evaluate the planned P1 intervention only once complete.

studies.name: Healing C3 qualification
studies.verdict: Composite works; extra agent adds no gain
studies.result: Qwen 37/60 correct, Jev 60/60, composite 60/60. All 23 Qwen errors were corrected. Qwen scored 0/20 in the refute class.
studies.sample: 60 paired engineering fixtures reusing six template families per class; 180 responses.
studies.reading: The composite clears its screen, but Jev alone matches it. There is no demonstrated incremental Qwen benefit.
studies.limit: Synthetic qualification is not generalization to clinical/research curation. The 600-case main comparison remains in progress.
studies.next: Require measurable benefit against Jev alone, including cost and anchoring, in the full comparison.

studies.name: Immune Response A3
studies.result: 16/16 valid episodes and 120 calls. All eight paired healthy-tick differences were zero. Every healthy-control episode unnecessarily redeployed the current version; the joint recovery/preservation gate failed.
studies.sample: Four constructed cases × two memory conditions = eight paired worlds.
studies.reading: Checking receipts did not induce restraint. This was a completed, valid adverse result.
studies.limit: No measured customer-health damage. Incident performance is at or near ceiling, limiting sensitivity to a receipt effect.
studies.next: Repair the demonstrated preservation prerequisite before interpreting larger treatment comparisons.

studies.name: Quorum of Mirrors Q1-02
studies.result: 16/16 valid responses, but 0/8 correct on graded full-lineage cases (requirement ≥7/8). All choices tracked copied-report majority.
studies.sample: Eight graded full-lineage cases; eight partial cases are ungraded.
studies.reading: Formatting is repaired; the model still counts correlated reports as evidence against independent-root truth.
studies.limit: Repetition, misleading prior choices and prompt wording are confounded. Historical S0 is not a controlled before/after comparison.
studies.next: Use exact lineage deduplication as a baseline and diagnose fixed-state failures before the committee study.

studies.name: Theseus execution D1
studies.verdict: Interface and compute change the result
studies.result: Strict scores: legacy 40/96, clean executor 82/96, keyed evidence 88/96, no notebook 89/96, one-case-per-call 96/96. The last arm alone clears the gate.
studies.sample: Three worlds; 144 calls and 480 dependent decisions.
studies.reading: The one-case interface is a useful engineering lead, not evidence of inherited culture.
studies.limit: It uses eight times the calls and 2.51 times the cost versus no-notebook batching. Legacy's 48 command-invalid outputs explain much of its strict deficit; post-hoc semantic matching gives 83/96.
studies.next: Test the qualified interface on fresh tasks and compare equal resources; retain original strict scores.

studies.name: Influence D3
studies.verdict: Complete forms still contain wrong facts
studies.result: 90/90 checklist fields filled, 76/90 correct. Every workflow made the same choices: 4/6 acceptable decisions and two avoidable deferrals.
studies.sample: Six diagnostic cases; repeated workflow measurements.
studies.reading: A consistency instruction did not improve factual interpretation. Schema completeness is not reasoning success.
studies.limit: No external-influence efficacy finding follows. D4 is unrun; D5 is prepared only.
studies.next: Test source-cited extraction and fixed policy arithmetic as separate components.

studies.name: Unfinished follow-ups
studies.result: At 08:11:40 UTC: budget Sonnet 1,533/2,880 outputs; Healing C3 160/600 cases; Market Opus first S1 bundle running with 17 planned; Scale XL preparing inputs with zero S1 answers; PC3 and compositional Q0-008 running.
studies.sample: Public hub snapshot. Counts are execution progress, not final scientific estimates.
studies.reading: Several substantial results are still collecting. A partial budget analysis exists, but incomplete cells are unsuitable as final policy rankings.
studies.limit: This view is a frozen review, not an automatically updating monitor. Hub done means execution ended and can include analysis, scripted or qualification jobs.
studies.next: Read the completed cohort, original endpoints and all failed/missing outcomes before drawing conclusions.

scope: Reviewed 50 registered experiment entries in the public hub; selected 14 consequential completed findings and diagnostics, plus unfinished follow-ups. Read current reports and plans, recomputed selected aggregate results and checked Qwen memory endpoints. This is not a full independent replay of every raw trace.
